problem: Prior semantic-map completion methods for ObjectNav (L2M, SSCNav, SGM) are deterministic/discriminative and ignore the uncertainty of indoor layouts, and generalize poorly to unseen scenes because training scenes have limited object-arrangement diversity. LLM-based methods need the LLM at inference, adding latency and memory cost.
motivation: Agents must imagine unobserved regions to find goals, but many plausible layouts exist for the same partial map, and densely annotated indoor datasets are small. Commonsense co-occurrence knowledge from LLMs can enrich training signals without needing the LLM at inference.
key_idea: Train a flow-matching model that directly maps a partial semantic map to a full semantic map whose unobserved regions are augmented with LLM-derived 2D Gaussian co-occurrence priors, distilling LLM knowledge into the flow model.
insight: The data-dependent coupling (partial map as source) beats a Gaussian-source conditional DiT (SR 41.5 vs 39.0 on MP3D) with fewer parameters and lower inference time. Scene segmentation gives the largest gain (SR 32.4→38.8), and the LLM prior adds a further +2.9 SR (→41.7). Flow matching matches MAE on MP3D but transfers better to HM3D (SR 35.9 vs 32.1, with RedNet in both), and a larger DiT-L does not help, likely overfitting on limited data.
method: LLM contextual prior: prompts an LLM (role, CoT, few-shot; scene→room→object hierarchy) for pairwise object distances d_ij and confidences c_ij; symmetrized into matrices D and C.

Gaussian prior construction: clusters observed objects, picks co-occurring candidates (d_ij≤τ_d or c_ij≥τ_c), places each candidate's centroid at distance d_ij from the observed object toward the nearest frontier, with σ from a linear map of confidence; summed isotropic 2D Gaussians form p_LLM.
Data-dependent coupling: source X0 = visible mask ⊙ GT map + small noise (Δσ=0.01) in unobserved areas; target X1 = GT map + λ·(unobserved mask)⊙p_LLM. Masks are simulated with FMM paths as in PONI.
Flow-matching training: DiT-B with OT linear interpolant X_t=(1-t)X0+tX1 and MSE velocity loss (X1−X0); no cross-attention conditioning is needed. Inference uses n Euler steps (saturates near n=96).

Scene segmentation mapping: back-projects RGB-D into a registered 3D point cloud, segments it at once with a Sparse UNet (Pointcept), and projects it to a BEV semantic map for consistent scene-level perception.

Imagination and navigation: crops and resizes the observed map to 256×256 (expansion ε), generates the full map, takes the argmax of the goal channel as a long-term waypoint, and navigates with an FMM local planner. New waypoints are sampled adaptively, only when the agent is too close to or too far from the previous one.

setting.backbone: DiT-B flow model (trained from scratch) + Sparse UNet scene segmentation; LLM (ChatGLM-4-plus / DeepSeek-R1 / GPT-4) used only offline for priors
setting.training_data: 400K sub-maps sampled per dataset (Gibson or MP3D) from GT semantic maps, with LLM-derived priors; the scene segmentation net is trained on the same benchmark scenes; HM3D is transfer-only (trained on MP3D)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + pose (GPS/compass), built into a 3D point cloud and BEV semantic map
setting.action_space: low-level move_forward / turn_left / turn_right / stop, via long-term waypoint + FMM local planner
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT full-scene semantic maps are used only in training)

results: GOAL reaches SR 83.5 on Gibson and 41.7 on MP3D, beating SGM (78.0 / 37.7) in SR, SPL and DTS. It also beats UniGoal (SR 41.0) and T-Diff (39.6) in MP3D SR, while its SPL is lower than SG-Nav and UniGoal. On HM3D transfer from MP3D it gets SR 48.8, above VoroNav (42.0) and PONI* (41.8).
limitations: Fixed-category semantic map channels prevent open-vocabulary generalization.
Training visibility masks are rectangular while the real agent's view is fan-shaped, which creates a train/test gap.
The adaptive waypoint policy and many Euler steps make correcting false positives slow; SPL gains are small and FPS is lower than PONI (1.2–1.8 vs 1.5–3.5).
